title: Open bank account
summary: Open a business bank account to separate personal and company finances — the first finance move for a company in any country. The US startup banks run fully-online applications with day-or-two approvals (the default flow below); the per-country rails and providers ride in the geo notes. KYC on the founders is universal; the tax ID the bank asks for is the local one (US: the EIN).

parts.title: Choose a bank
parts.guidance: Compare institutions eligible for the company’s entity type, jurisdiction, owners and activity. Examine currencies, payment rails, approval controls, accounting connections, fees and support. Identify the legal account provider and how funds are held or protected under the offered arrangement. Use current eligibility and account terms to narrow the choice before starting an application.

options.title: Default — Choose a bank
options.summary: Verify the institution’s eligibility requirements and the legal entity offering the account. Compare payment capabilities, access controls, fees, service limits and applicable deposit protection with the company’s operating needs. Check significant claims against the actual account terms, then select the account to take into onboarding.

options.title: UK/EU - multi-currency account
options.summary: For a UK or EU company, compare providers supporting its ownership and business profile. Check available currencies and account details, regulatory status, how balances are held, conversion costs and payment permissions. Match those terms to expected collections and spending, identifying restrictions that would affect operations before choosing the multi-currency account.
options.when: The company is incorporated in the UK or EU - the US neobanks don't onboard it

parts.title: Complete the online application (company details, tax ID — US: EIN — and founders)
parts.guidance: Complete the bank application from the formation records and company profile, checking name, addresses, applicable tax identifier, ownership and signers. Resolve inconsistencies or eligibility questions with the company officer responsible for the account. That authorized applicant submits the information and attestations and handles any further documents the bank requests.

parts.title: Upload founder ID and formation documents (KYC)
parts.guidance: Collect the identity and formation documents the bank actually requests, checking legibility, validity and consistency with the application. The authorized applicant submits them through the bank’s verified secure channel with the relevant individuals’ permission. Resolve rejected or incomplete documents and limit unnecessary copies of personal identity material.

parts.title: Wait for the bank to open the account (1–2 business days)
parts.guidance: Follow the application in the bank’s official channel, respond to outstanding questions and use the bank’s current processing estimate. Once approved, check the account name, payment features, access and any conditions before using it. The account administrator should know what is operational and what still needs activation.

verify.how: The dashboard shows account and routing numbers and a small inbound test transfer clears.

parts.title: Connect the bank feed to the books
parts.guidance: Have the bank-account administrator authorize the supported accounting connection for the intended accounts. Map each feed to the correct ledger account and choose an import date that avoids duplicating existing entries. Compare a sample with the statement and reconcile the first import. Establish who handles failed syncs or access changes before relying on the feed at close.

verify.how: Transactions from the account appear in the books feed within a day.

metadata.supportReason: The application and KYC upload are online forms (no public API); approval is a bank-side wait. Once open, the account connects to the books over the bank API.

geoNotes.summary: Open a UK business account once (or while) the company registers at Companies House — Wise Business and Airwallex both fully serve UK-registered companies per the committed geo spike, and challenger/high-street onboarding is the same KYC/UBO conversation as the US flow.

The real path is a current account with an Indian bank once incorporation documents and PAN exist — the geo spike found Airwallex doesn't onboard Indian-registered businesses and Wise's India business offering is receive-from-abroad only, so domestic banking is bank-first, KYC in person or video.

German companies are served through the EEA fintech rails — Wise (via Wise Europe) and Airwallex's Europe entity both onboard German entities with local IBANs, per the committed geo spike — alongside the traditional Hausbank route; expect the notarized formation documents in the KYC pack.

French companies open on the same EEA rails (Wise Europe, Airwallex Europe — both judged available) or with the Paris-native Qonto, whose onboarding is built around French formalities — a new SAS's dépôt de capital commonly happens at the same provider that becomes the operating account.
